title: World Country Languages
description: Independently compiled factual reference data for the current CLDR country-language relationship manifest. Each record represents one approved country or area and language relationship after alias normalization and base-row collapse.
methodology: SoftData compiled the current CLDR country-language relationship manifest from Unicode CLDR JSON release 48.2.0. Territory rows were mapped to approved world-countries-and-areas identifiers, aliases were normalized, script-qualified rows were collapsed to their approved base-language identifiers, and only relationships whose final language id exists in world-languages were published. The mandatory base-row-wins rule was applied when choosing relationship status: an exact base-language row for a country and language pair overrides script-qualified rows, while a script-qualified row may supply the status only when no base-language row exists. The approved remaps were fat -> ak, sh -> sr-Latn -> sr, tl -> fil and tw -> ak. Required conflict outcomes are gb / en -> official, hk / zh -> used, in / hi -> official, me / sr -> used, mo / zh -> used and sn / ff -> official_regional. The resulting dataset contains 1,289 unique country/language pairs, covers all 248 approved country or area ids, has zero orphaned country ids and zero orphaned language ids, and is sorted by country_area_id then language_id.
update_policy: Review against a deliberately selected CLDR release; do not silently upgrade the pinned source release.
known_limitations: This is a CLDR-derived territory-language relationship set, not a complete census of languages spoken in each country or area. The used status is not a legal-recognition claim.

normalization.base_row_wins_rule: When a base-language row and a script-qualified row collapse to the same country/language pair, the exact base-language row supplies the status. A script-qualified row can supply the status only when no base-language row exists.
